clue.text: Now that could be a thingummybob!

indicators.note: says the letters of the opening words might be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone points at a mystery object and wonders whether this is the gadget they were after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges NOWTHAT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are vague names for a small object whose proper name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Nobleman says: "Hello! Happy to turn up with a ring"

parts.note: hello is the greeting hi

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: happy means glad
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A nobleman greets someone and announces he is glad to arrive bearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' makes DALG from GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a Spanish gentleman of the lower nobility.

clue.text: The meal is half gone? What's the idea?

indicators.note: only the front half of the word meal is left once half has gone

explanation.surface: Someone finds their dinner half eaten and demands an explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the central idea of a piece of work, so the question asks what that subject is.

clue.text: Roy sets about getting an aphrodisiac

definitions.note: singular in the clue but the plural shellfish together count as the one supposed love food

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man called Roy goes looking for something to boost his love life.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish are famously reputed to stir desire, the classic example of a food said to arouse.

clue.text: Novelist sees five hundred join a crowd

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A writer watches a large number of people join a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist, so her surname stands for the writer.

clue.text: Gather for a cigarette

definitions.meaning: to gather something up by rolling it, as with a sleeve or map
a hand-rolled smoke made from loose tobacco

explanation.definitionFit: Rolling something up gathers it in, and the hyphenated noun names a cigarette rolled by hand.

clue.text: Possesses raised lacework with burns on

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a web is a fine lacy network
itches means burns or tingles irritatingly

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a piece of lace while their skin stings.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess someone in the supernatural sense is to bewitch or cast a spell over them.

clue.text: Waits for ships carrying goods initially

indicators.note: carrying means holding one piece inside another

parts.note: liners are large passenger ships

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of goods

explanation.surface: Someone stands around while cargo vessels are loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints LINEERS, not a word; the wordplay and the count of seven give LINGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to wait about or stay on longer than needed.

clue.text: Aunt Sally falling about with family

parts.note: falling about is laughing helplessly
stock is lineage or family descent

explanation.surface: A relative called Sally is in fits of laughter alongside her relations.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing at a dummy head, hence a figure everyone mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a target for ridicule, someone everyone mocks.

clue.text: The advantage of retired gentlemen

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone asks what benefit there is in being a man of leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a reversal signal, but the run sits forwards across 'retired gentlemen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge means holding a slight advantage over a rival.

clue.text: To chant about glory is believing

indicators.note: about means placed around another piece

parts.note: to chant is to sing
to glory in something is to wallow in it

explanation.surface: Singing hymns of praise is a sign of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallowing a story means accepting it as true without question.

clue.text: Claim member is more than half way through a drink

indicators.text: is more than half way through
indicators.note: the limb goes into the drink after two of its three letters

parts.note: ale is a drink
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone says a limb has got deep into a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim something without proof.

clue.text: Gloomy letter, only half read, seen as a challenge

parts.note: gaunt can mean grim or bleak

indicators.note: only the first half of the word letter is kept

explanation.surface: A depressing letter, abandoned halfway through, is taken as a provocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing down this glove was a challenge to fight, so the word stands for a challenge.

clue.text: Suit and shirt torn in revolution

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a coup is a sudden overthrow of government

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clothes get ripped during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing beside 'shirt', but it means wooing; 'torn' scrambles the shirt's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay suit to someone is old-fashioned wooing, the same as courtship.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic uncle gets involved with tart

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A relative grudgingly becomes entangled with a woman of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reluctant is unwilling and lacks enthusiasm.

clue.text: Grand party-giver showing spirit

parts.note: G is short for grand, as in a thousand pounds
a host gives a party

explanation.surface: A lavish party host appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Upset, needing second capsule

parts.note: a capsule is a pill

explanation.surface: Someone distressed needs another tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a drink is to spill it.

clue.text: Introduce referee, having to stride around

indicators.note: around means the stride goes round the referee

parts.note: a pace is a stride

explanation.surface: A referee must walk about the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to introduce it with opening remarks.

clue.text: Attacker in silver-grey nearly getting Ross to retreat

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: nearly drops the final letter

parts.note: taken in full before trimming

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: a man's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: An assailant in a silvery-grey outfit almost makes Ross back off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' turns GREY into GRE; 'to retreat' makes SSOR from ROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is one who attacks first.

clue.text: Thought highly of, but always dipping into wine

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside another piece

parts.note: red is red wine
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone admired but forever drinking claret.
explanation.definitionFit: To be revered is to be deeply respected and admired.

clue.text: It takes work, under a month, to find a sea creature

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: Oct is short for October
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: Finding a marine animal takes effort for less than a month.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is an eight-armed sea animal.

clue.text: Remain standing up in time for an argument

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up reads the word upwards

parts.note: to be is to remain, as in let it be

explanation.surface: Someone stays upright for a while before a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns the two-letter word for remain upwards, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument between opposing sides.

clue.text: Pains will penetrate rigid trunk

indicators.note: penetrate means get inside another piece

parts.note: set means fixed or rigid
aches are pains

explanation.surface: Pain will spread through a stiff torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests the body, but here it is a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's sea chest is a trunk for belongings on a voyage.

clue.text: Trumpets for five of mother's sisters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a mother's sisters are aunts

explanation.surface: Brass instruments are bought for five maternal relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to boast about it, which is to vaunt.

clue.text: This official must take us with her

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An official is told to bring a woman along with the group.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher is an official who shows people to their seats or keeps order.

clue.text: Island where angry ruler receives injury

parts.note: mad means angry
an aga is an Ottoman commander or ruler
a scar is the mark of an injury

explanation.surface: A place where a furious monarch gets hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is a large island off the east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Operations at hospital for limps

indicators.note: at means placed next to the hospital piece

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Surgery at a hospital leaves patients walking unevenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an injured leg hops or limps along.

clue.text: King catches the ball

indicators.note: catches means holds the next piece inside

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's play
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a leather is slang for the ball, which is made of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket balls are leather-covered, so the material names the ball itself.

clue.text: Today's clothing, which may help delivery people

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
dress is clothing

explanation.surface: Modern clothing that could be useful to couriers.
explanation.definitionFit: Postal workers rely on the destination written on a parcel to deliver it.
